project.name: strata-mcp
project.description: Local memory layer for AI agents — a persistent-memory MCP server that indexes AI coding-assistant conversation history into a local SQLite/FTS5 database with Gemini vector embeddings, exposing search and recall tools over MCP, plus a REST transport for game-engine NPCs. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Excludes node_modules, build artifacts, tests, and dev files from the Docker build context to keep image layers small and reproducible.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Node.js 22 Alpine build: a builder stage compiles TypeScript via npm run build, then a slim runtime stage copies dist/ and node_modules, runs as the non-root strata user, exposes port 8080, and launches the MCP server via dist/cli.js serve.
nodes.languageNotes: Multi-stage build pattern separates compile-time deps (python3/make/g++ for native modules like better-sqlite3) from the runtime image, which only carries libstdc++ alongside the compiled output. HEALTHCHECK is configured for orchestrator liveness.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what Strata is: a persistent-memory layer for AI coding assistants that captures decisions, bug fixes, and patterns as structured knowledge and serves them back through the Model Context Protocol. It positions Strata against Mem0 and LangMem, advertises 81.1% on LongMemEval-500 with a BM25 + vector + RRF stack, and previews the local SQLite / Cloudflare D1 / GCP deployment targets and the quality-gated evaluator pipeline. Read this first to get the project's purpose and vocabulary before touching code.

tour.title: Process Entry & CLI
tour.description: Every invocation begins here. src/index.ts is the shebang binary that constructs the MCP server via createServer() and connects it over stdio, while src/cli.ts dispatches all strata subcommands (search, store-memory, migrate, serve, distill, deploy) and chooses the stdio, HTTP, or REST transport. Together they are the doorways through which Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and game engines reach the engine you'll explore next.

tour.title: The MCP Server Factory
tour.description: src/server.ts is the heart of the system and the export downstream packages (strata-pro, strata-team) depend on. createServer() wires the SQLite index, search engine, stores, embedders, watchers, and the agent loop together, then registers all 15 community MCP tools and returns the configured server plus its dependencies. Building on the entry points from Step 2, this is where the runtime object graph is assembled — the natural root of the dependency tree.
tour.languageLesson: This is a factory function returning an object of wired dependencies rather than relying on module-level singletons. Accepting an optional { dataDir } lets the same factory power single-tenant stdio and per-user multi-tenant instances with isolated caches and databases.

tour.title: Central Config & Tunables
tour.description: src/config.ts has the second-highest fan-in in the codebase — almost everything imports it. It centralizes every empirically-tuned parameter: BM25 k1/b, RRF fusion constants, chunk sizes, recency decay, and importance weights, all optimized via the AutoResearch eval suites. Understanding this file early explains why the search and ranking code in later steps reads the way it does, and CONFIGURATION.md documents the environment variables that override these defaults at runtime.

tour.title: Ingesting Conversations
tour.description: Strata's defining feature is auto-indexing transcripts from multiple AI tools. The parser registry detects which tool produced a session and selects a compatible parser; session-parser.ts then turns raw Claude Code, Codex, Aider, Cline, or Gemini logs into normalized turns ready for knowledge extraction. This is the front of the pipeline — where external history becomes structured input.
tour.languageLesson: A registry + interface pattern (parser-interface.ts) decouples the engine from any single transcript format. Adding support for a new assistant means implementing the interface and registering it — no changes to call sites.

tour.title: The Quality-Gated Knowledge Pipeline
tour.description: This is what makes Strata different from a vector dump: every candidate memory passes through deterministic quality gates before storage. knowledge-extractor.ts pulls candidate facts from parsed turns, knowledge-evaluator.ts applies the actionability/specificity/relevance gates, dedup.ts removes near-duplicates, and importance.ts scores what survives. The result is a clean, auditable knowledge base rather than a growing pile of everything — see the evaluator-pipeline doc for the gate semantics.

tour.title: The Knowledge Store
tour.description: Surviving knowledge entries land in the KnowledgeStore, a high-fan-in module that is the canonical write/read surface for extracted memory and another key export consumed by strata-pro and strata-team. Building on the pipeline from Step 6, this store persists evaluated entries with their history and exposes them to the search layer. It sits at the boundary between the knowledge logic and the physical storage backends explored next.

tour.title: Storage Backends (SQLite / D1 / Postgres)
tour.description: Strata owns its storage end-to-end across three deployment targets. database.ts resolves the data directory, opens the better-sqlite3 connection, and initializes the schema; factory.ts selects between SQLite and D1 at runtime; and the d1/ and pg/ index modules assemble the same store interfaces over Cloudflare D1 and Postgres. The shared interfaces directory defines the contract every backend implements, which is why a memory written locally behaves identically at the edge.

tour.title: The Database Schema
tour.description: The migration SQL defines the data model that backs every backend from Step 8: conversation documents, extracted knowledge entries with history, session summaries, embeddings, the entity graph, evidence gaps, and analytics. Reading the schema makes the store interfaces concrete — the columns here map directly to the KnowledgeStore and document store APIs you just saw.
tour.languageLesson: Migrations are forward-only and numbered (0001, 0002, ...) so the schema evolves deterministically across SQLite, D1, and Postgres. FTS5 virtual tables provide the full-text index that the BM25 channel in the next step queries.

tour.title: Hybrid Search & Ranking
tour.description: This is the retrieval engine the README benchmarks. sqlite-search-engine.ts fuses four channels — FTS5 full-text (BM25), vector similarity, knowledge, and entity — while semantic-search-bridge.ts supplies the 3072-dimensional Gemini embeddings (with graceful keyword-only fallback when no API key is set). result-ranker.ts performs the reciprocal-rank fusion, recency/importance boosts, and per-session capping that turn raw channel hits into the final ranked results. The benchmarks doc reports how this stack reaches 81.1% on LongMemEval.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combines independently-ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) across channels, avoiding the need to calibrate incomparable BM25 and cosine scores onto a single scale. The rrfK constant lives in config.ts from Step 4.

tour.title: Quantized Embedding Storage
tour.description: Owning the storage layer lets Strata ship features a wrapped vector DB cannot. turbo-quant.ts combines Hadamard rotation, Lloyd-Max scalar quantization, and bit-packing into a single compact blob so 3072-dim embeddings fit affordably across SQLite, D1, and Postgres. This is the TurboQuant algorithm the README highlights as not yet standard in production vector databases — a concrete payoff of the end-to-end storage ownership from Step 8.

tour.title: The MCP Tools Surface
tour.description: These are the 15 tools agents actually call, registered by the server factory from Step 3. store-memory.ts writes a vetted memory through the pipeline of Steps 6-7, search-history.ts runs the hybrid search of Step 10, and find-solutions.ts targets past error fixes. They are the contract every MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI) speaks to — the thin, well-defined layer over the engine you've now seen end to end.

tour.title: Transports: stdio, HTTP & Game-Engine REST
tour.description: The same server is exposed three ways. http-transport.ts serves Streamable HTTP on /mcp for single-tenant deployments; multi-tenant-http-transport.ts adds an LRU per-user database pool for SaaS use behind an auth proxy; and rest-transport.ts is the v2 game-engine surface with two-tier player tokens, world/NPC scoping, and a dialogue-shaped /recall endpoint for Unity, Godot, and Unreal. This is how the one engine reaches local IDEs, cloud agents, and game NPCs alike.

tour.title: Local Distillation Pipeline
tour.description: Strata can route its entire LLM pipeline — extraction, conflict resolution, summarization — through Gemma 4 running locally via Ollama, keeping Gemini only as a safety-net fallback. provider-factory.ts auto-selects the provider based on config, hybrid-provider.ts implements the local-first strategy with output validation and a circuit breaker, and cli/distill.ts drives setup/test/activate. The local-inference doc ties it together, and accumulated training data feeds eventual model distillation.
tour.languageLesson: The circuit-breaker pattern trips after consecutive local failures and routes to the frontier provider, preventing a flaky local model from stalling the pipeline while still preferring on-device inference when it works.

tour.title: Tests, Evals & CI
tour.description: The capstone: how Strata stays trustworthy. Integration tests like cross-tool-memory.test.ts index synthetic Claude Code and Gemini sessions side by side and assert cross-tool retrieval, the distillation-e2e eval drives the full pipeline and judges answers against frozen fixtures, and the CI workflow runs build, test, security scanning, and license checks on every PR. Together they guard the contract that every step of this tour relies on.
tour.languageLesson: YAML CI workflows use `on` triggers and parallel `jobs` (build-and-test, security-audit, license-check). Frozen eval suites are never modified during optimization, so score changes reflect code changes rather than a moving target — the AutoResearch discipline referenced in config.ts.
